text:
The Avalanche and Mammoth unveiled their Winter Classic uniforms today, for New Year's Day at Rice-Eccles Stadium. Tonight's meeting is indoors, and the weeks behind them could hardly differ more. Colorado lost Nathan MacKinnon (30 points, out until about Dec. 12) and Cale Makar (23 points, about Nov. 28) last week and answered with a 4-1 win in Montreal, their best chance share of the last five games at 70% of the expected goals (the quality of chances). Utah is winless in six (0-3-3), and after Karel Vejmelka was pulled Monday against Vancouver, the net goes to Sebastian Cossa.

That goaltending change is the story for the Mammoth. Cossa is at .864 in eight games, 4.9 goals below what the shots against him were worth. Mackenzie Blackwood, across the ice, is at .905 and 2.4 above. It's the clearest gap between these teams, and it's the reason a Utah side that has taken 58% of the five-on-five expected goals this season (Colorado: 53%) sits four points back of the Avalanche when our expected-points count has them dead level at 27.4.

Colorado's patchwork is holding. Brock Nelson has stepped into MacKinnon's spot beside Martin Necas and Artturi Lehkonen, Lehkonen has goals in three straight and now plays on the top line, top power play and top penalty kill, and Sam Malinski played 24:19 with Makar out. Nazem Kadri hasn't scored in five games despite 3.5 expected goals, so the chances are there. Utah is short too, without Dylan Guenther, Nick Schmaltz and John Marino; Vincent Trocheck has absorbed more than 24 minutes a night and is one assist from 400 for his career, and Logan Cooley has 14 points in his last ten with the chances to back it up.

Our numbers have it close: 3.49 expected goals for Colorado, 3.18 for Utah. Watch the penalty box. The Mammoth take 4.7 penalties a game, and Colorado's power play produces 0.84 expected goals a night against a Utah kill that allows 0.76. With Utah at 66% to make the playoffs and the losing streak at six, this is a night that matters more to the home side.
headline: A Winter Classic preview, with Utah's net in question
